findings.title: Glossary rows 35 and 36 define 'highest root' and 'root poset' by facts of simply laced boards, false on B, C, F, G
findings.location: site/src/content/pages/glossary.mdx:318-323 (row 35, dfn highest-root) and :326-331 (row 36, dfn root-poset); route /glossary/#highest-root, #root-poset (preview and release); linked from M1 beats 3 and 4 and M2
findings.claim: The glossary drops M1's hypothesis ('a board of finite type with single roads', E8) and defines 'highest root' as 'On a board of finite type, the root population at which no mutation raises any city.' It defines 'root poset' as 'The positive root populations of a board, arranged by total population, with an edge from one to another wherever a mutation raises a city.' On B, C, F, G the first picks out two populations and the second is not the root poset.
findings.expected: SPEC 2.6: 'Highest root theta: the root population of largest form value that no mutation raises; unique [V]'. F13: on B, C, F, G, Kostant's game from a short node ends at the highest short root. SPEC 4 T2 and 2.16 call the raising-edge picture the Hasse diagram of the root poset only 'on a simply laced board of finite type'.
findings.observed: Oracle (redteam-RT-09-p6-oracle.py): the root populations raised by no mutation are two on each board: B2 (1,1),(1,2); B3 (1,1,1),(1,2,2); C3 (1,2,1),(2,2,1); F4 (1,2,3,2),(2,3,4,2); G2 (2,1),(3,2). The highest short root satisfies the glossary's definition of the highest root. On B2 the raising edges are (1,0)->(1,2) (a rise of 2) and (0,1)->(1,1), while the root poset's covering relations are (1,0)<(1,1), (0,1)<(1,1), (1,1)<(1,2). On G2 the raising edges include (0,1)->(3,1).
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of f07eec6 plus the reproducer: npm ci --prefer-offline; npx vitest run --project site-unit site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-09-p6-glossary-history.test.ts -t 'P6-RT-09-01'. Both tests fail at the assertion that quotes the definition (source, no build needed). Oracle values: python3 redteam/RT-09/redteam-RT-09-p6-oracle.py reference.
findings.specRef: SPEC 2.6 (Highest root row); 2.7 F13; 4 T2 ('On a simply laced board of finite type every such edge raises by 1 and the picture is the Hasse diagram of the root poset. On B, C, F, G a rise of 2 or 3 occurs'); 2.16; RT-09 attacks 1, 15, 31
findings.proposedFix: Row 35: 'the root population of largest form value at which no mutation raises any city (on a board with single roads, the only one)'. Row 36: scope to 'a board of finite type with single roads', as M1 beat 4 does.

findings.title: The history page states Donnelly and Eriksson's finite-type theorem without the hypothesis that roads run both ways; the one-way board contradicts it
findings.location: site/src/content/pages/history.mdx:67 (timeline entry 2008, data-entry Don08, last sentence); route /history/ (preview and release)
findings.claim: 'Donnelly and Eriksson use the game to prove that a connected graph with whole-number road counts is a Dynkin diagram of finite type exactly when some start that has no negative number and is not all zeros gives a game that ends' is false for a graph with a one-way road. The site defines such boards and offers them in the editor.
findings.expected: SOURCES.md [DE08]: 'Theorem 2.1: a connected integer-weighted graph ...' (the integer-weighted graphs of that literature have roads both ways). M3 beat 7 states the same theorem as 'a connected board with roads both ways is of finite type exactly when its numbers game ends from some start with a positive number and no negative one'. SPEC 2.1: on a one-way board 'none of the theory of this section applies'; 2.11.
findings.observed: The one-way board [[2,0],[-1,2]] (one road from city 1 to city 2, none back) is connected and has whole-number road counts. classify gives kind 'one-way', class none, so it is not of finite type. Yet legal play from (1,0), a start with no negative number and not all zeros, ends at (-1,-1) after 2 moves. This is the oracle's play() (word 1, 2; fired 1, 1) and also the engine's play (status 'ended', moves 2).
findings.reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline; npx vitest run --project site-unit site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-09-p6-glossary-history.test.ts -t 'P6-RT-09-02' (fails on f07eec6); oracle: python3 redteam/RT-09/redteam-RT-09-p6-oracle.py reference (section 'history, entry 2008').
findings.specRef: SOURCES.md [DE08]; SPEC 2.1 (bidirected; one-way board), 2.11; site M3 beat 7; RT-09 attack 1 (a fact of bidirected boards stated for all boards)
findings.proposedFix: Write 'a connected graph whose roads all run both ways, with whole-number road counts, ...', as M3 does.

findings.title: Glossary row 64 says the shape of a Wythoff polytope depends only on which nodes are ringed; SPEC says its combinatorics
findings.claim: 'Its shape depends only on which nodes are ringed' is false of the shape. Two orbits with the same ringed nodes have the same face counts but different ratios of edge lengths, which the glossary's own 'uniform' entry and M7 rely on.
findings.expected: SPEC 2.14: 'The convex hull of the orbit of lambda is a polytope whose combinatorics depend only on which nodes are ringed'; edge squared length 2 d_i a_i^2.
findings.observed: Oracle (redteam-RT-09-p6-wythoff.py): B3 (0,1,1) and (0,2,1) both have f-vector (24, 36, 14). Their squared edge lengths are {2, 4} and {2, 16}, ratios 2 against 8.
